thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: elevated 5xx rate observed from canary cluster 'east-1-canary' for /v1/chat/generate — error: malformed payload when writing to messages table :rotating_light:
maya (SRE): i'm looking. initial spike 1:12pm UTC, sustained. rolling windows show increased locks on messages_update job. canary traffic 10% of rollout but 5xxs up ~18%
sam (oncall): i'm paged, taking lead. tags: release-stage:canary, service:message-writer. is there a migration running?
eli (DB): yes — async job `migrate_message_payload_type` kicked off at 12:03. it's converting `payload` TEXT -> JSONB with validation. seeing repeated `invalid input syntax for type json` on some rows. that causes transaction aborts and retries, holding locks.
tasha (release): rollout 12:00 included payload protobuf change + db migration. feature flag `payload_v2_enable` gated to 10% (canary) but the flag check was added after the writer path in the release — so writer still tries v2 for canary. awaiting confirmation but that matches stack traces.
maya (SRE): ok primary mitigation options: 1) flip flag off globally (kill switch) 2) rollback release in k8s 3) quiesce migration job and resume after a compatibility fix. which is fastest?
eli (DB): safest: pause the migration and apply an on-the-fly compatibility shim. fastest: kill flag. downside: flag service uses Redis cluster that the release updated the client for — the new release may be reading a different key namespace, so kill may not reach canary pods.
sam (oncall): tasha can you verify flag naming? if kill won't reach canary, fallback to rollback. we need <5m to reduce customer impact.
tasha (release): confirmed — flag key prefix changed (`payload_v2:` -> `payload:v2:`) in this deploy. old flag UI won't affect new pods. that's my mistake, sorry.
maya (SRE): understood. plan: 1) block migration job immediately, 2) rollback canary deploy to previous image, 3) assess impacted customers and warm rollback to primary clusters if needed. eli, can you stop the migration? sam and tasha run rollback.
eli (DB): stopping migration now — killing background worker `migrate_message_payload_type` (pid 43721). command:```bash
supervisorctl stop migrate_message_payload_type || kill -9 43721
```
eli (DB): confirmed stopped. tail of migration logs shows last failing row id=74291: `payload='\x9f...'` — invalid JSON bytes. will snapshot problematic rows to S3 for later cleanup.
tasha (release): starting k8s rollback for deployment message-writer in east-1-canary to image `message-writer:v1.49` (previous). command:```bash
kubectl -n prod rollout undo deploy/message-writer --to-revision=47
```
tasha (release): rollback initiated. monitor pods... new pods ready 3/3 on 12:21:34 UTC
sam (oncall): observed 5xx rate falling in canary from 18% -> 2% within 90s of rollback. great.
maya (SRE): good. please keep migration stopped. eli, what's customer impact now? any writes lost?
eli (DB): migration stopped mid-run; it was doing transforms with transactional updates. some rows processed succeeded, others aborted and retried, but client retries surfaced 5xxs. no durable data loss expected. we'll compile a list of affected customer IDs from logs — prelim estimate: ~12 orgs saw increased error rates during 12:03-12:21 window. prep customer comms draft.
sam (oncall): logging ticket for customer-impact and alerting: incident-ticket-#8702. linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/db-migration-failure
maya (SRE): next steps: - keep migration stopped - create compatibility shim: writer will accept legacy payloads (attempt parse JSON then fallback to text) - create targeted fix to migration to skip/mark malformed rows and move them for offline remediation - re-run migration on small batches behind feature flag after fix
tasha (release): i'll also open an immediate hotfix PR to adjust flag key namespace back to old key so we can use flag in case we need partial rollouts. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/4821
eli (DB): i'll export malformed rows to s3://incidents/migration-2951234567/ and add a `migration_errors` table with raw payload & error_reason so we can reconcile.
maya (SRE): handoff: sam — oncall until 13:00 UTC. jana — you're next for 13:00-20:00, please pick up and validate migration is stopped and rollback stable.
jana (oncall-next): acknowledged. i'll validate and run the postmortem checklist.
incident-bot: INC:8702 acknowledged. severity: sev2. paging log updated.
maya (SRE): status update 12:35 UTC: canary rollback complete, 5xx rate back to baseline, migration job stopped, identifying affected customers. will keep thread open until migration is fully remediated and a safe re-run plan exists.
sam (oncall): summarizing customer impact for ops: 12 customers saw elevated write errors for ~18 minutes. no data loss, higher retry rate and some UX errors. recommended comms: targeted email + support banner for those orgs.
eli (DB): note for post-incident: add preflight validation step for async migrations that verifies JSONB conversion candidate rows produce valid JSON; add 'dry-run' mode to migration job.
tasha (release): retrospective: flag namespace change should have been part of rollout checklist. adding a step to verify kill-switch reachability for canaries.
maya (SRE): assigning follow-ups: - DB: export & reconcile malformed rows (eli) - Release: hotfix flag key & rollback automation (tasha) - SRE: improve migration preflight and runbook (maya) - Customer ops: draft comms (sam)

maria (support): adding note — support drafted emails, awaiting list of affected org ids, ready to send on sign-off.

maya (SRE): closing interim update 12:52 UTC. will reopen if signals worsen. final handoff to jana at 13:00. thanks all for quick coordination :thumbsup:
